extracted.intended_audience: petitioners, patent owners, and practitioners involved in AIA proceedings before the PTAB (patent litigators and representatives)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the USPTO/PTAB interim processes for Director discretionary denial/referral of institution in AIA proceedings, including which discretionary considerations are relevant, filing windows and brief limits, P-TACTS paper types and filing steps, and examples of fact patterns supporting referral or denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whether PTAB or another forum has already adjudicated validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether PTAB or another forum has already adjudicated validity or patentability of the challenged patent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties are permitted to address this consideration in discretionary-denial briefing. It is one of the listed discretionary factors the Director may weigh when deciding whether to deny institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes in law or new judicial precedent affecting patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether there have been changes in the law or new judicial precedent issued since issuance of the claims that may affect patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may raise this point in briefing; the Director may consider such changes when exercising discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strength of the unpatentability challenge
rubrics_metrics.description: The strength of the unpatentability challenge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may argue regarding the merits/strength of the challenge in discretionary briefing. FAQ 8 notes the Director will consult USPTO personnel with relevant technical expertise when parties present arguments regarding the strength of the merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent of petition’s reliance on expert testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent of the petition’s reliance on expert testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may address this in briefs as a discretionary consideration; high reliance on expert testimony is a factor the Director may weigh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settled expectations of parties (length of time claims in force)
rubrics_metrics.description: Settled expectations of parties, such as the length of time the claims have been in force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This consideration can weigh for or against institution; parties should explain the practical expectations (e.g., how long claims have been enforced) and any persuasive reasons why an IPR is or is not appropriate despite settled expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compelling economic, public health, or national security interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Compelling economic, public health, or national security interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may raise these categories of public-interest considerations in discretionary briefing for the Director to consider.

rubrics_metrics.name: Any other considerations bearing on the Director’s discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: Any other considerations bearing on the Director’s discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list of discretionary considerations is non-exclusive; parties may present other relevant facts and arguments for the Director’s holistic review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner discretionary denial brief filing window
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner may file a discretionary denial brief within 2 months after the PTAB issues a Notice of Filing Date Accorded (NFDA) (or a Notice of Defective Petition) and the PTAB accepts a patent owner’s Mandatory Notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This timing rule applies for proceedings where the deadline to file a preliminary response (POPR) occurs after March 26, 2025. Use the new P-TACTS paper type for timely filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitioner opposition to discretionary denial brief filing window
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner may file an opposition brief within 1 month after the due date for the patent owner’s discretionary denial brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should track the patent owner brief due date carefully; the petitioner’s opposition window is one month after that due date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director decision process and outcomes (bifurcation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions on whether to institute an AIA trial are bifurcated between discretionary considerations (decided by the Director) and merits/non-discretionary considerations (decided by a Board panel if referred).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director issues a discretionary decision based on a holistic review and may (1) deny the petition (no trial instituted) or (2) refer the petition to the Board to handle the case in normal course; if referred, a Board panel will issue an institution decision addressing merits and other non-discretionary considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director consultation with senior judges and technical personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director (in consultation with at least three senior PTAB judges) determines whether discretionary denial of institution is appropriate and will consult USPTO personnel with relevant technical expertise when parties present arguments regarding strength of the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FAQ 8 explains technical-expertise consultation; the review team is smaller (10–12) to promote consistency and efficiency versus >100 judges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director may consider additional circumstances beyond parties' briefs (FAQ 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: While the Director ordinarily will rely on facts and circumstances the parties raise in the briefs, the Director will consider additional circumstances where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: to maintain consistency with already-issued discretionary decisions; where there are facts and circumstances within Office or Office operations the parties are not in a position to raise; or where there are facts and circumstances in the record or the public domain relevant to the determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: New 20‑page limit for discretionary briefs (effective Sept. 1, 2025)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the interim processes memorandum, briefs were previously permitted up to 14,000 words; starting Sept. 1, 2025, all briefs are limited to 20 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow general formatting requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 42.6(a). Parties may request additional pages by demonstrating good cause and emailing Director_Discretionary_Decision@uspto.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of new P-TACTS paper types for discretionary briefing
rubrics_metrics.description: The PTAB introduced two new paper types in P-TACTS: PO Discretionary Denial Brief and PET Opposition to Discretionary Denial Brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For timely consideration, parties should use these new paper types. Filing steps: log into P-TACTS → My Docket → open case viewer → +Add → File Other Document modal → select the appropriate paper type → enter required fields (red asterisk) → Add to List → Submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of fact patterns supporting referral to the Board
rubrics_metrics.description: Representative fact patterns that support referral rather than discretionary denial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided: apparent material error during examination (e.g., Padagis US LLC v. Neurelis, Inc.); an early challenge to patentability in a PGR, close in time to examination and before expectations in patent rights are strongly settled (e.g., Multi-Color Corp. v. Brook & Whittle Ltd.); evidence the challenged patent has never been commercialized, asserted, marked, licensed or otherwise applied in petitioner’s particular technology space (e.g., Shenzhen Tuozhu Tech. Co., Ltd. v. Stratasys, Inc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of fact patterns supporting discretionary denial
rubrics_metrics.description: Representative fact patterns that weigh against referral (support denial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided: unfair dealings when inventors advocate for unpatentability of their own patent (e.g., Tessell, Inc. v. Nutanix, Inc.); settled expectations based on length of time patent in force when petitioner provides no persuasive reasoning why IPR is appropriate (e.g., Dabico Airport Sols. v. AXA Power ApS); non‑exclusive examples that rebut a patent owner’s settled‑expectation claim (e.g., change in law or a patent that has not been commercialized).

rubrics_metrics.name: Locating Director Discretionary Decisions on PTAB website
rubrics_metrics.description: How to find Director Discretionary Decisions on the PTAB website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select 'All PTAB decision data' → Documents tab on the 'PTAB Decisions' page → search for 'Director Discretionary Decision' under 'Document type' → select both 'Director Discretionary Decision: Refer' and 'Director Discretionary Decision: Deny' → Apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA proceedings timeline and statutory limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Key timeline milestones for AIA proceedings under the interim processes (preliminary and trial phases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant timeframes shown: Petition/NOFDA → PO Preliminary Response (3 months max, by statute) → PO Request for Discretionary Denial (2 months after NFDA) → Petitioner Opposition (1 month) → Director Decision on discretion (1 month) → Decision on institution on merits (Board). Trial-phase timing: standard sequencing of PO Response & MTA, Pet. Reply, PO Sur-Reply, discovery periods, motions on evidence, oral hearing on request; Final Written Decision no more than 12 months (by statute).

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and content topics in FAQs/webpage
rubrics_metrics.description: The FAQs (now retired) and the interim processes webpage provide information about availability/timing, conflicts of interest, procedures/processes, new paper types for filing briefs, briefing requirements, and requests for rehearing or Director Review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office has retired the FAQs and published an interim processes webpage as a guide; parties should consult that page and Director_Discretionary_Decisions@uspto.gov for questions.
